{{nihongo|'''Hitsuji Shrine (Nagoya)'''|羊神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Owari Province]].

'''Hitsujinja Shrine''' (ひつじじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|Q80434|qid=Q80434}}{{ill|Nagoya|Q11751|qid=Q11751}}{{ill|Kita-ku, Nagoya|Q1207964|qid=Q1207964|lt=Kita Ward}}{{ill|Tsujichō|ja|辻町 (名古屋市)|qid=Q17215607|lt=Tsujimachi}}. It is identified with the “Hitsujinja Shrine” listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}} under {{ill|Owari Province|Q514506|qid=Q514506}}{{ill|Yamada district, Owari|Q11470699|qid=Q11470699|lt=Yamada District}}.

=== Overview ===
Until the {{ill|Edo period|lt=Edo period|qid=Q184963}}, it was called '''Shinmei''' and served as the {{ill|Ujigami|Q767655|qid=Q767655}} (guardian shrine) of {{ill|Kasugai district|ja|春日井郡|pl|Powiat Kasugai|zh|春日井郡|qid=Q11513576}}{{ill|Tsujichō|ja|辻町 (名古屋市)|qid=Q17215607|lt=Tsujimura}}. The year of foundation is unknown, but as a {{ill|Munafuda|ja|棟札|zh|上樑記牌|qid=Q8008834}} (ridge tag) from the {{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} era remains, it is presumed to date to before the {{ill|Middle Ages|Q12554|qid=Q12554}}. The early Edo-period document '{{ill|Kanbunmuramuraoboegaki|Q137766629|qid=Q137766629}}' records it as “Tsujimura... Shinmei, previously exempt.”

It was identified by {{ill|Amano Sadakage|Q6535030|qid=Q6535030}} and others as the “Hitsujinja Shrine” of Yamada District in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}, and this has been the prevailing theory since the Edo period {{Sfn|Aichi Prefectural Association of Shinto Shrines|1992|p=3}}. The basis for this identification is an old tradition stating that because the location was Tsujimura, and “Hitsuji” (sheep) was written as “Fire Tsujī,” the character “fire” was taken to form the place name “Tsujī” {{sfn|Aichi Prefectural Association of Shinto Shrines|1992|p=3}}. However, {{ill|Tsuda Masanari|Q22123474|qid=Q22123474}}, a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=local historian}} of the late Edo period, proposed an alternative theory that the original Hitsujinja Shrine was the Tenjin of {{ill|Seko|ja|瀬古 (名古屋市)|qid=Q29902337|lt=Seko Village}} (present-day Takamuta Shrine).

It is also said that the shrine’s name derives from a residence once located here that belonged to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tago Hitsujidayū}}, who ruled {{ill|Kōzuke Province|Q1054838|qid=Q1054838}}{{ill|Tago District, Gunma|ja|多胡郡|sr|Област Таго|qid=Q11431032}} and stopped here when traveling to the capital at Nara <ref name="由来"/>.
